title: Types of books
source: User-provided workbook photo, manually transcribed; Word File German translations suggested separately

entries.description: A book with several brief tales in it
A book about the life of a real person
A story written to be performed on stage
Poems
A book that explains what words mean
A collection of texts by different writers
The text for a film
A long book that tells an invented story
A story told in pictures with speech bubbles

entries.example: I expected the food to be good, but I was really disappointed.
entries.description: Sad because something was not as good as you hoped

entries.example: The rollercoaster ride was so thrilling that I couldn't stop screaming.
entries.description: So exciting that your heart beats fast

entries.example: Before I buy a book, I always read the blurb on the cover first.
entries.description: The short text on the back of a book

entries.example: Her smile was heartwarming and made my day better.
entries.description: Making you feel happy and full of love

entries.example: My nephew is the son of my sister.
entries.description: The son of your brother or sister

entries.example: The story is set in a castle in the 19th century.
entries.description: The story ___ ___ ___ London in 1900. (It happens there.)

entries.example: This book is a tearjerker and might make you cry.
entries.description: A very sad story or film that makes you cry

entries.example: It's a brilliant book - you will simply love it.
entries.description: Excellent; really great

entries.example: Reading this book was delightful. A joy of a story.
entries.description: Very pleasant

entries.example: The concert was an electrifying experience. The audience was filled with excitement.
entries.description: So exciting that it fills people with energy

entries.example: The book is very entertaining. You won't be able to put it down.
entries.description: Fun and interesting

entries.example: The last scene was hilarious and really made me laugh.
entries.description: Extremely funny

entries.example: She is a terrific writer - she has a lot of talent.
entries.description: Fantastic; wonderful

entries.example: Despite a lot of difficulties, he finds true love in the end.
entries.description: He went out ___ the rain.

entries.example: She loves reading fiction because she likes to escape into other worlds.
entries.description: Stories about invented people and events

entries.example: Tom always wears goggles when he swims.
entries.description: Glasses that protect your eyes when swimming

entries.example: John took a week off work to sort himself out.
entries.description: To deal with your own problems and feel OK again

entries.example: He's in a spot of bother with the police.
entries.description: A small problem; some trouble (British)

entries.example: She's playing on the field with her wee brother.
entries.description: Small or little (Scottish)

entries.example: Sputnik wears a big jumper and a leather helmet.
entries.description: A warm piece of clothing for the top of your body; sweater

entries.example: He wore a traditional Scottish kilt to the wedding.
entries.description: A skirt worn by men in Scotland

entries.example: He nodded in agreement when she explained the plan.
entries.description: To move your head up and down to say yes

entries.example: He was scratching at windows and doors with his long nails.
entries.description: To rub something with your nails

entries.example: The antagonist in the movie tried to stop the hero.
entries.description: The character who fights against the hero

entries.example: The book's plot was full of unexpected twists and turns.
entries.description: What happens in a story

entries.example: The protagonist is the main character of a story.
entries.description: The hero or main person in a story

entries.example: The setting of the story was a small village in the mountains.
entries.description: The place and time where a story happens

entries.example: We need to complete the project within the agreed timeframe.
entries.description: The period you have to finish something

entries.example: The villain tried to take over the city, but the hero stopped him.
entries.description: The bad guy in a story

entries.example: The trilogy is action-packed with an adventure on every page.
entries.description: Full of exciting events

entries.example: The movie's captivating plot kept the audience on the edge of their seats.
entries.description: Holding your attention completely

entries.example: There was never a dull moment in the book. It was really exciting.
entries.description: Boring

entries.example: Go and buy a copy immediately. The book is a must-read.
entries.description: A book you really have to buy and look at; it's essential

entries.example: I finished the novel in one night. It was a real page-turner.
entries.description: A book so exciting you can't stop reading
